subject: Design recommendation: multipath connector for on-prem LLM access
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@acmesecure.com>, netops@acmesecure.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Design recommendation: multipath connector for on-prem LLM access

Hi Michael / NetOps team,

Thanks for the call earlier — following up with a clear recommendation and the reasons why we think a multipath connector (Primary: PrivateLink, Secondary: S2S VPN fallback, with optional peering for specific low-latency subnets) hits your reliability and compliance goals while keeping operational overhead reasonable. Attached is a one-page diagram and a short SOP checklist.

Key recommendation (short):
- Primary path: AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints) into a dedicated Redwood Private control plane interface.
- Secondary/failover: Site-to-site IPsec VPN from your on-prem gateway into a dedicated fallback VPC.
- Selective peering: VPC Peering for low-latency batch jobs between a small set of subnets only if you accept broader routing exposure.

Why this mix?
- PrivateLink gives the tightest surface-area controls (no route table changes, explicit endpoint policies) which matches your compliance asks.
- VPN provides a predictable fallback channel that is easier for your ops to test during DR drills.
- Peering is powerful for latency-sensitive workloads but increases blast radius; we recommend limiting peering to a single analytics subnet and only after we have observed traffic patterns for 2–4 weeks.

Operational notes:
- We will publish a short handshake runbook (attached sop-handshake-checklist.xlsx) that includes IP ranges, cert fingerprints, and a mutual test plan.
- Expect a 2–3 week delivery window for PrivateLink endpoint provisioning + firewall rule validation. VPN tunnel can be run in parallel and validated within 48–72 hours.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you have a preferred NAT/egress pattern for the endpoint VPC (SNAT via a central egress vs. per-customer egress)?
2) Are there stricter egress IP allowlists for auditing services (we can publish predictable IP blocks)?

Attachments: diagram-multipath-anchoring.pdf (diagram), sop-handshake-checklist.xlsx (mutual-action checklist)

Next step: if this captures your needs we propose a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) and a kickoff call Tues 5/12 to provision a PrivateLink test endpoint and a VPN tunnel.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying points from NetOps before we commit to the MAP: 

1) We prefer peering avoidance where possible due to our segmented routing policy, so PrivateLink-first aligns nicely.
2) For the VPN fallback: can you confirm whether the VPN will carry KV cache replication traffic (we would prefer to restrict KV replication to the primary path only)?
3) Firewall questions: we run a strict deny-by-default posture and will need the exact TCP ports and cert CNs to open.

Also attaching our internal network inventory (attachment stub: acme-net-inventory.csv) — please call out any CIDR conflicts.

If you can answer the KV replication question and provide the IP/port list we can schedule the kickoff.

—Michael

Subject: Re: Design recommendation: multipath connector for on-prem LLM access

Thanks Michael — quick technical clarifications below.

On KV cache replication:
- Short answer: we recommend restricting KV cache population and high-sensitivity state replication to the PrivateLink path only.
- Rationale: VPN tunnels are typically subject to MTU and jitter that can impact large, synchronous replication. For replication we rely on our secure control plane channel (mTLS over PrivateLink).

Ports/IPs/certs for firewall:
- Outbound from on-prem to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs: TCP 443 (mTLS) to a small set of predictable ENI IPs — we'll publish those IPs in the MAP and keep them stable for the duration of the pilot.
- VPN fallback endpoints: ESP/UDP-500/UDP-4500 for IPsec IKEv2, plus TCP 22/9200 only if you opt into pipeline diagnostic sockets (disabled by default).
- We will provide PEM fingerprints and CNs for our mutual TLS certs in the SOP.

Peering notes (why we suggested a small peering use-case):
- Use-case: batch inference jobs that require <5ms RTT and carry large payloads (e.g., model weight loading during warm starts).
- Controls: peering limited to non-sensitive analytics subnets, explicit route table tags, and a short review window (30 days) after which we recommend removal unless you sign off.

Operational test plan (high level):
1) Provision PrivateLink endpoint (Redwood creates ENI, Acme allows the ENI IPs).
2) Validate mTLS channel and run KV population smoke test (read-only).
3) Provision VPN; test failover by simulating PrivateLink outage (cut connections at endpoint level).
4) Optional: enable selective peering and run latency/throughput benchmarks for batch jobs.

Attached: small checklist added to the SOP. Let us know suitable times for the kickoff on Tue 5/12 or Wed 5/13.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Design recommendation: multipath connector for on-prem LLM access

Michael — perfect, thank you for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and assignments: 

Action items (who / what / by when):
- Redwood (Jonas + Kimberly): publish final MAP and IP/port/cert list by EOD 2026-05-12. Deliverables: diagram-multipath-anchoring.pdf, sop-handshake-checklist.xlsx, and a short test plan doc (Drive link in metadata).
- Acme NetOps (Michael): confirm a 2-hour maintenance window on Tue 2026-05-18 for PrivateLink ENI validation and provide the primary on-prem gateway public IP for VPN pre-shared-key exchange.
- Redwood (Sean): stand up the VPN endpoint and share IKE parameters (target: 2026-05-14).

Decision summary (for the record):
- Primary = PrivateLink (mTLS) for control and KV-sensitive traffic.
- Secondary = IPsec S2S VPN for failover and lower-sensitivity traffic.
- Peering = optional, limited, and gated — not part of pilot unless Acme requests it in writing after telemetry.

If that aligns, we'll send a MAP document and a DocuSign for the pilot SOW that locks in the provisioning timeline.

Cheers,
Jonas
